title: Bruce Henderson - Wikipedia
content: | Known for | Founder of Boston Consulting Group |. **Bruce Doolin Henderson** (April 30, 1915 – July 20, 1992) was an American businessman and management expert. He founded Boston Consulting Group (BCG) in 1963 in Boston, Massachusetts and headed the firm as the president and CEO until 1980. Henderson was born on a farm in Nashville, Tennessee on April 30, 1915. In the fourth grade, he enrolled in the Peabody Demonstration School (PDS) and remained there until his high school graduation in 1932. In 1959, Henderson left the company to join the consulting firm Arthur D. Little, Henderson accepted a challenge from the CEO of Boston Company to create a consulting arm for the bank, operating as a subsidiary under the name Management and Consulting Division of the Boston Safe Deposit and Trust Company. Henderson stepped down from his role as the president and CEO of Boston Consulting Group in 1980.

title: BCG History - The History of Boston Consulting Group
content: BCG began not as another management consulting firm but as a pioneer of bold, new approaches to running a company. One of the many legacies left by Bruce Henderson, BCG’s founder, is the importance of always challenging the status quo. ## Bruce Henderson’s Ideas and BCG Perspectives. From the beginning, Bruce Henderson’s passion for ideas was the firm’s mark of distinction. His ideas and writings reveal a visionary who excelled at challenging the status quo, a brilliant thinker, and a man of action, driven by a strong sense of purpose. In 1964 he developed a new approach to marketing a consulting firm: *Perspectives*, brief and highly provocative essays on strategy. The concept of time-based competition, first introduced by BCG in the 1980s, is a demonstration of the power of time management. When Bruce Henderson founded BCG, he envisioned that it might someday change the world. With true insight and the ability to transform it into action, BCG has driven real change in organizations and fulfilled Henderson’s vision.

title: M. Eric Johnson | Bruce D. Henderson Professor of Strategy | What Makes A Firm Competitive? Wisdom from BCG’s Bruce Henderson
content: Wisdom from BCG’s Bruce Henderson. This year I have been reflecting on the legacy of Bruce Henderson. A Vanderbilt alumni and Owen School professor, Bruce was a pioneer in the business world, founding the Boston Consulting Group and participating in the creation of the management consulting industry. To celebrate the hundredth anniversary of his birth, BCG launched an Institute in honor of its founder and followed up this summer with a new book on strategy. I was a new Assistant Professor at Owen and would often look to see if there was a light on in his office when I stopped by the lounge for a cup of coffee. Working on the Owen School’s strategy this year, I turned to Bruce’s teaching on competitive advantage. At a lecture delivered at Owen in the early 1980s, he argued that organizations must have a particular mix of characteristics that provide a unique advantage in the marketplace.

title: BCG launches research unit: Bruce Henderson Institute
content: *The Boston Consulting Group has yesterday, on the day that founder Bruce Henderson would have turned 100, launched a new research Institute. More than 50 years down the line, The Boston Consulting Group has become one of the most influential management consultancies of the globe. In honour of the hundredth anniversary of the firm’s founder\*, BCG has launched the ‘Bruce Henderson Institute’, an entity that will seek to develop ideas at the cross-section of strategy and execution. In a period of immense challenges for the global economy, the establishment of the Bruce Henderson Institute exemplifies BCG’s commitment to stay on the cutting edge of ideas and to translate those ideas into meaningful business impact.”. **Boston Consulting Group** is not a United Kingdom partner of Consultancy.org. **Boston Consulting Group** is a Local partner of Consultancy.org in Netherlands.
